statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-69806 is an elevation of privilege issue in the .NET SDK's dotnet watch: its Aspire server service (AspireServerService) exposes information through certain arguments, which can enable code injection. Microsoft's advisory lists Linux installations of the .NET 10 SDK in the 10.0.1xx feature band (10.0.100 to 10.0.110) and the 10.0.3xx band as affected (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/442, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167); the CVE record lists the .NET 10.0 runtime before 10.0.12 (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806), and the .NET 10.0.12 release notes, whose 10.0.1xx SDK is 10.0.112, list this CVE (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.12/10.0.12.md). The change that makes dotnet watch pass the project's launch environment through the hot reload agent instead of the process environment is "Set project environment variables using Hot Reload agent" on the dotnet/dotnet release/10.0.1xx branch (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/c92c2c9607fd7dc5580bd737ccfddac6ea6b02b2); it is in the v10.0.112 source tag and later, and not in v10.0.111, although the advisory names 10.0.111 as the patched SDK. No DHI build carries SDK 10.0.111, so the boundary does not depend on that difference. DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Its only .NET SDK is the 10.0.1xx SDK in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, from SDK 10.0.102 in the first build to SDK 10.0.115 in 10.0.15-r0, and dotnet-watch.dll ships only there, one copy per build and architecture. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. The builds before 10.0.13-r0 carry SDK 10.0.102 to 10.0.110 (there is no 10.0.11 or 10.0.12 build for Alpine 3.23), all in the affected range. Extracted and inspected dotnet-watch.dll from the dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap package of 10.0.10-r0 (Alpine 3.24, x86_64), 10.0.12-r0 (Alpine 3.24, x86_64 and aarch64) and 10.0.13-r0 (Alpine 3.23, x86_64 and aarch64): the 10.0.110 copy has no SetEnvironmentVariables message type, while the 10.0.112 and 10.0.113 copies carry the SetEnvironmentVariables request and EnvironmentVariablesSet response that the fix adds, and all of them contain AspireServerService and ProjectLauncher. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0, the first published build whose SDK carries the fix.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-69806 is an elevation of privilege issue in the .NET SDK's dotnet watch: its Aspire server service (AspireServerService) exposes information through certain arguments, which can enable code injection. Microsoft's advisory lists Linux installations of the .NET 9 SDK in the 9.0.3xx feature band (9.0.300 through 9.0.316, fixed in 9.0.317) as the affected .NET 9 SDKs, and does not list the 9.0.1xx band (https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/442). The CVE record names the .NET 9.0 runtime before 9.0.20 as the affected product (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806), but the advisory places the vulnerable code in the dotnet watch Aspire service of the 9.0.3xx SDK, and the 9.0.1xx SDK released with .NET 9.0.20 (9.0.121) does not contain that service. The fix changes how dotnet watch passes the project's launch environment to the application (https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/commit/d4099745c1b346ea90cfee17f2361a4cd0bbf5b9). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, which builds the 9.0.1xx SDK band: the SDK in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap is 9.0.113 to 9.0.124 across the builds. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. In the 9.0.1xx sources the dotnet watch project does not include the Aspire service (the dotnet-watch project file imports the AspireService shared project in the 9.0.3xx band, for example at v9.0.300 and v9.0.316, but not at v9.0.113 or v9.0.124), and none of the dotnet-watch.dll copies shipped in the dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap packages contains any Aspire code or the AspireServerService type, while each holds the expected hot reload code. No package contains a Microsoft.WebTools.AspireService assembly or nupkg. So the vulnerable Aspire server code is not in this owner.
